column1: # THE COUPLING EXEMPTIONS (CLAUDE.md, Design rules; project/Coupling.scala `Exemptions`, scripts/ci/coupling_ratchet.py):
# the classes and packages the two limits -- class fan-out (`limit fanout`) and package distance D (`limit distance`,
# packages of `limit distance-min-types` types or more) in test/resources/coupling-baseline.tsv -- do not hold, and the
# declared contracts a class's fan-out counts as ONE dependency. A class or package past a limit with neither a frozen
# baseline row nor a row here fails the push; `scripts/coupling-report --update` never admits it. A row added or loosened
# here lands only in a commit carrying `Coupling: <why>` (the ratchet checks it); a row dropped needs none.
# pattern: a class or package name; `*` matches any run of characters (dots too); `p.*` also matches `p` itself.
#   root        fan-out and distance: the composition roots wire everything and nothing depends on them
#   registry    fan-out: data tables (venue rosters, scraper catalogues) that name one entry per class they list
#   foundation  distance: the bottom layers every package rests on -- stable and concrete on purpose (D near 1 is right)
#   config      fan-out: the typed-config root, which resolves every setting into its typed value in one place
#   contract    (column 3: the contract's name) the classes matching `pattern` are its USERS: their fan-out counts every
#               member of that contract they use as one dependency
#   member      (column 3: the contract's name) `pattern` is one of the contract's member types -- at most 8 a contract
#               (scripts/ci/coupling_ratchet.py), and adding or dropping one carries `Coupling: <why>` like any loosening
#   contract-size  (pattern: a contract's name; column 3: a number) a contract declared before the 8-member cap,
#               grandfathered at that size: it may not grow, and raising the row is a loosening
# column 3, for the exempting kinds: `exempt`, or a number -- a limit of the class's own, above the shared one.

column5: the composition roots (AppLoader, WorkerMain, AppComponents and the modules.wiring / modules.webwiring traits): every collaboration is wired here (DIP), so their fan-out is the application's size, and their D is a top layer's
command-line programs built from the whole stack like a composition root (FilmwebDiff, RosterAudit)
the review answers' command-line program (`web/runMain services.review.ReviewLabelsCli`): its main wires the mirror client, the answer store and every country's review source like a composition root
a city's or chain's venue roster: one entry a venue, each naming the scraper class that reads it -- data, its fan-out is its row count
a country's scraper catalogue: one entry a source, each naming its client class -- data, its fan-out is its row count
the Polish venues' registry over the city rosters: one reference a roster
the Polish towns in scrape order: one reference a town's venue roster (pl.venues.*Venues) -- data, its fan-out is its row count
the city registry: its companion lists every city and page of every country (one reference a city object or page row type, City.all the union) -- data, its fan-out is its row count
the country registry: one case object a country, each naming its cities, pages, aliases and picker groups -- data, its fan-out is its row count
the typed-config root: every environment variable is read here once and resolved into its typed setting (typed config conventions), so it names every setting type
the domain data every layer reads: stable (I near 0) and concrete (A near 0), as values are
generic utilities and the HTTP and Mongo layers, below everything: stable and concrete
typed configuration values, read by every layer: stable and concrete
the title text as a pure function library (TitleNormalizer, FormatTags): stable and concrete, nothing to abstract
a scraper's side of the scrape contract (CLAUDE.md: a new cinema is a new CinemaXClient on it): the twelve types every scraper is written against are one dependency, not twelve
the contract's entry point: what a scraper is
the shared parse helpers every scraper reads its page with
slots folded into the films a scraper returns
a scraper's per-film detail page reader
what a detail fetch came back with
what a detail page reads into
a film's own fields within it
the fetch a scraper is handed

a task handler's side of the task contract (TaskWorker dispatches a claimed Task to the TaskHandler for its TaskType and reads back a HandlerOutcome): the four types every handler is written against are one dependency, not four, as the scrape contract's are for a scraper
the contract's entry point: what a handler is
the claimed task a handler is handed
the type a handler is registered for

grandfathered: declared (2026-11) before the 8-member cap -- what a scraper is written against really is these twelve types (the scraper's entry point and parse helpers, the films and screenings it returns, the fetch it is handed); split it only along a line a scraper does not cross

the web tier's side of the served schedule (the controllers, their view models and markup builders, MovieControllerService): the schedule it renders is one model read together, one dependency, not six. Worker code using these types (the read-model projector, share cards) counts them one by one
one film's schedule in a city, the unit the pages render
the read model's film: its identity, ratings and metadata
a film's own fields within it
the venue a screening is at

the resolver core's side of its vocabulary contract: the eight immutable value types every stage of a resolve reads together (a listing, its key, its evidence and evidence node, a candidate, the query that found it, its scoring and denial) count as one dependency. Scoped by name to the resolver core (candidate generation, families, scoring, acceptance, the constraint edges and solver run, the decisions, the incremental model and its index), never the projection, the measures, the staging, the agreement stage or the adapters
one listing as its venue published it: the resolve's input
a listing's key: what every decision, edge and family names its listings by
listings of identical evidence, the unit a resolve scores and links
a node's merged facts, as the measures read them
a film a node has an evidence path to, with its record
a candidate question a node asks: what found a candidate
a candidate as a node's evidence scored it
why a node's evidence rules a candidate out

the identity projection's side of its vocabulary contract: the seven immutable value types every step of a projection reads together (the index of the listings, stored films and clusters, the scope one projection drafts, a listing as projected, a film drafted and as written, the plan to write, and its regroupings) count as one dependency. Scoped by name to the projection (indexing, scoping, drafting, keys, venue slots, guard, plan, write, drift and tick), never the resolver core, the measures, the agreement stage, the listing intake or the other adapters
what a projection reads off the listings, the resolution and the stored films before it drafts: listings by key, previous films, clusters
the films one projection drafts, compares and writes: its changes closed over what a draft reads
one published listing as the projection holds it: the listing and its row and showtimes digests
one film of a projection before its key is chosen: counter, inherited id, listings, record
a film as the projection writes it: id, counter, title, year, key, record, listings
a projection ready to write: the films, the ids retired, the FilmId-map additions, the regroupings
how the films moved between two projections: merges, splits, moves, fresh and retired ids
